tagline: Leading Membership Warehouse Club Operator in Eastern United States
hero_kpi_rationale: This KPI is the Hero because it reflects the company's operational performance in its membership warehouse club retail sector, enabling assessment of comparable store growth beyond portfolio expansion.

kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.description: The company's net sales increased by 4.6% in 2025 compared to 2024, rising from $20.05 billion to $20.96 billion
kpis.signal: Sales growth driven by traffic growth, portfolio expansion, and growth in food and perishables divisions

kpis.name: Comparable Club Sales
kpis.explanation: Sales from clubs open for at least 13 months
kpis.description: Comparable club sales increased by 1.0% in 2025 compared to 2024, with merchandise growth of 2.6% partially offset by a 1.6% decline in gasoline sales
kpis.signal: Growth in comparable club sales driven by merchandise growth, partially offset by lower gasoline prices

kpis.name: Membership Fee Income
kpis.description: Membership fee income increased by 9.5% in 2025 compared to 2024, rising from $456.5 million to $499.8 million
kpis.signal: Growth driven by increased acquisition, retention, and penetration of premium membership segments, as well as rate increases in January 2025

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Company gross margin excluding gasoline and membership fees
kpis.description: The company's merchandise gross margin remained stable in 2025 compared to 2024
kpis.signal: Stable merchandise gross margin despite inflationary pressures and pricing adjustments

kpis.name: Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
kpis.explanation: Company selling, general and administrative expenses
kpis.description: Selling, general and administrative expenses increased by 6.4% in 2025 compared to 2024, rising from $2.96 billion to $3.15 billion
kpis.signal: Increase due to labor, occupancy, and operational costs related to new store openings and higher depreciation expenses

risks.title: Dependence on Economic Conditions
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned in the first section of risk factors, with strong language on direct impact on consumer behavior. The company is highly dependent on economic health to maintain member spending. The Macro category is heavily weighted.

risks.title: Fluctuations in Gasoline Prices
risks.score_rationale: The risk is detailed with direct effects on comparable sales and margins. The text emphasizes price volatility and its impact on quarterly results. Central position in the 10-K.

risks.title: Inflation and Cost Pressures
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly linked to margin and sales, with mention of cost pressures that cannot be passed through to consumers. Warning language on inflation volatility. Critical Macro category.

risks.title: Dependence on Member Renewals
risks.score_rationale: The business model relies on membership fees. The document emphasizes the renewal rate (90%) as a key indicator. A decline would threaten the stability of recurring revenue.

risks.title: Supply Chain Disruptions
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned in the context of the company's ability to meet demand. Although crucial, the language is less alarming than for macro risks. Mid-level positioning in the document.

risks.title: Technology and Digital Investments
risks.score_rationale: Investments in digital systems (BOPIC, ExpressPay, etc.) are strategic. The text highlights their role in customer experience, but without explicit technical risk. Moderately weighted Technology category.

ai_positioning.summary: BJ's company does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
